basis: Anterior pituitary inflammation defines endocrine disease; xanthomatous histology alone does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: pathogenesis is uncertain; inflammatory infiltrates alone do not establish autoimmune, immune-mediated or infectious disease.

basis: Defining myopathy/respiratory phenotype; lung hypoplasia 2/3. Cleft palate 3/3; urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis 1/3, renal hypoplasia 1/1. Ocular findings omitted at cap; tiny cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory insufficiency defines the syndrome, with direct lung hypoplasia in 2/3 rather than respiratory muscle weakness alone.

basis: Severe CNS hypomyelination; amyotrophy (80-99%) is secondary to neurologic motor impairment, without primary muscle disease. Nystagmus is neurologic; respiratory failure 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent amyotrophy reflects neurologic motor impairment; direct skeletal muscle pathology is not established.

basis: Ear defects 80-99%; oral clefts and ocular defects 30-79%. Micrognathia 30-79% supports skeletal involvement; nail hypoplasia (30-79%) omitted at cap as less severe.

decisions.dermatologic: none: nail hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of more consequential jaw hypoplasia.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital mandibular hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%; retained ahead of nail hypoplasia under the four-axis cap.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; aortic stenosis 2/2, tongue/dental malformations 2/2, and intellectual disability or cord compression 1/2 support additional axes; very small samples.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: macroglossia and microdontia each occur in 2/2, supporting persistent developmental involvement of tongue and teeth, both within this axis.

basis: Mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm; perivascular growth and proposed pericytic differentiation do not by themselves establish a blood-vessel neoplasm or vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: perivascular growth alone does not establish a vessel-wall origin or direct vascular disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: classified as a mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm, fitting the connective-tissue axis without another specified organ of origin.

basis: Cutaneous hemangiomatosis is vascular proliferation in skin, defining skin and blood-vessel disease. Associated extracutaneous features and their frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas are blood-vessel proliferations; vascular tissue is the lesion's origin, while cutaneous location also supports dermatologic.

basis: Autoimmune skin and muscle disease; ILD occurs in roughly 30-50% in several anti-SAE cohorts, with substantial geographic variation. Dysphagia can reflect muscle involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: direct interstitial lung disease reaches roughly 30-50% in several anti-SAE cohorts, although estimates vary considerably by population.

basis: CNS malformations define the disorder. Strabismus/oculomotor apraxia (30-79%) reflect central motor dysfunction; direct eye disease or visual tissue damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent strabismus and oculomotor apraxia reflect abnormal central eye-movement control; direct ocular damage is not established.

basis: Corrosive dermal exposure causes chemical burns/necrosis; systemic poisoning disrupts energy metabolism with acidosis. Additional CNS, cardiac or renal injury lacks established >=30% frequency.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: corrosive skin burns and necrosis are characteristic direct injury in the usual dermal exposure pattern of monochloroacetic acid poisoning.
